costGuide.labourLine: Fitting an A17DTJ typically takes 8-10 hours at £65-£75/hr (independent) - confirm exact labour when comparing quotes.
paragraphs: What genuinely moves the price on the A17DTJ is the fuel system variant - some units run Denso injection, others Bosch, and they are not directly interchangeable without ECU and wiring changes . Timing belt history and DPF condition also affect the value of a used unit. See our full reconditioned engine cost guide.

failures.title: Vauxhall A17DTJ Engine Problems - What Actually Fails

items.title: Injector seal leakage (Black Death) - 2009-2013 units
items.whatHappens: The rubber injector seals corrode and leak combustion gases past the injector, causing carbon buildup around the injector pocket. This is the most common complaint on the A17DTJ . If left unaddressed, the carbon can seize injectors in the head, turning a £400 seal replacement into a £1,500+ head repair.
items.repairVsReplace: Seal replacement is viable when caught early - the injectors can usually be extracted without head damage. If the carbon buildup is severe and injectors are seized, the head work cost often pushes the repair into "consider replacement" territory.

items.title: DPF and EGR clogging - all years, urban-use cars
items.whatHappens: Like most modern diesels, the A17DTJ's DPF requires regular motorway runs to regenerate. Short journeys cause the DPF to clog, triggering limp mode and increased fuel consumption . The EGR valve also clogs from soot recirculation.
items.repairVsReplace: DPF cleaning (£400-£800) is viable if the unit isn't physically damaged. EGR valve cleaning or replacement (£200-£500) is straightforward. If the DPF is saturated beyond recovery, replacement or a full engine assessment is needed.

items.title: Fuel system issues - Denso-equipped variants
items.whatHappens: The A17DTJ was fitted with either a Denso or Bosch fuel system. The Denso systems are known for SCV (suction control valve) and injector issues, especially with cheap fuel filters . Symptoms include poor starting, lack of power, and eventually refusal to start .
items.repairVsReplace: SCV replacement (£200-£400) and proper filter maintenance can resolve fuel system issues. Injector replacement (£300-£800 per injector) is viable but expensive.

failures.goodYearsLine: The A17DTJ was produced from 2009 to 2011 at the Polish plant . The engine itself is mechanically robust - forum reports indicate examples reaching 300,000 miles with proper servicing . The key is fuel filter discipline (change every 10,000 miles with OEM-quality filters) and regular motorway runs for the DPF .

variants.title: A17DTJ and Related 1.7 CDTi Codes - Which One Is in Your Car?
variants.intro: The 1.7 CDTi family spans Euro 4 (Z17) and Euro 5 (A17) variants. The A17DTJ is one of several sub-codes - knowing which matters because fuel systems, ECU calibrations and wiring looms differ. - Fitted to: Astra J, Zafira B, Meriva B, late Astra H - Key technical difference: Replaced the Z17DTJ. Euro 5 emissions compliance with DPF, updated ECU calibration. 110 hp (81 kW) output . - Sub-code-specific failure note: Shares the family failure pattern above. Denso fuel system variants more prone to SCV issues . - Interchange note: Physical swap with other 1.7 CDTi codes is possible, but getting it running requires matching ECU, wiring and likely the entire engine harness . - Fitted to: Astra H, Zafira B - Key technical difference: Predecessor to the A17DTJ. Euro 4 emissions - no DPF on some variants. Same base Isuzu block, different ECU calibration. - Sub-code-specific failure note: Shares the same injector seal and fuel system concerns as the A17DTJ. - Interchange note: Not a direct ECU-compatible swap with A17DTJ without a full electrical package . - Fitted to: Astra H, Zafira B, Meriva A - Key technical difference: Higher-output variant of the same Isuzu block. 125 hp (92 kW) . - Sub-code-specific failure note: Shares family pattern. Higher output means more stress on the turbocharger. - Interchange note: Higher output tune may require different turbo and injector calibration.

relatives.description: The Euro 4 version of the same Isuzu 1.7 CDTi block, fitted to Astra H and Zafira B from 2007-2009. It shares the same base architecture but lacks the DPF on some variants and runs a different ECU calibration. Not a direct ECU-compatible swap without the full electrical package. [Z17DTJ engine page pending - not in current inventory]

The 1.6 CDTi introduced from 2014, co-developed with PSA/Ford. It replaced the A17DTJ on Astra J, Zafira Tourer C and later models. More refined, but with its own set of DPF and AdBlue concerns. [B16DT engine page pending - not in current inventory]

The higher-output 125hp variant of the same Isuzu block. Fitted to Astra H, Zafira B and Meriva A. The extra power means a different turbocharger calibration and injector map. Same fuel system and DPF concerns as the A17DTJ. [A17DTR engine page pending - not in current inventory]

variants.closing: The engine code is stamped on the cylinder block near the timing belt cover. On Vauxhall/Opel, check the V5C logbook or the build sticker in the service book (often shows "LPV" for A17DTJ) . Enter your reg above and we'll confirm for you.

buyingGuide.title: Buying a Replacement A17DTJ - What to Choose

options.label: Used
options.body: A used A17DTJ makes sense for lower-value Astra H or Zafira B hosts (£2,000-£4,000 vehicle value) where a reconditioned unit would exceed the car's worth. Insist on documented fuel filter history - cheap filters kill the Denso fuel system . Factor in a timing belt service if the seller can't prove it was done within 150,000 miles. Used engines guide

options.label: Reconditioned
options.body: A proper recon on the A17DTJ addresses the injector seals (new seals and decarb), DPF and EGR cleaning, timing belt replacement and a full fuel system check. This is the right call for Astra J, Meriva B or Zafira B hosts worth £5,000-£12,000 where the car justifies the spend. Reconditioned engines guide

options.label: Rebuilt
options.body: A full rebuild on the A17DTJ is rarely needed - the short block is robust and typically outlasts the fuel system and ancillaries. Consider a rebuilt unit only for a low-mileage, high-spec car you plan to keep long-term, or if the original has suffered a DPF-induced oil dilution failure. Rebuilt engines guide

buyingGuide.supplyFitLine: Supply-only or fully fitted - our network of UK diesel specialists can fit your A17DTJ with a nationwide warranty. Supply and fit service
buyingGuide.vehicleValueNote: The A17DTJ sits in volume Vauxhall models with wide value ranges. For an Astra H or early Zafira B worth under £2,500, a reconditioned engine at £1,500-£2,800 supply-only is borderline - consider a good used unit with history or evaluate scrap value first. For an Astra J or Meriva B worth £4,000+, a reconditioned unit is financially sound.

mainEntity.name: What's the difference between A17DTJ and Z17DTJ?

acceptedAnswer.text: The Z17DTJ is the earlier Euro 4 version (2007-2009), fitted to Astra H and Zafira B. The A17DTJ is the Euro 5 successor (2009-2015) with updated ECU calibration, DPF on all variants and revised emissions hardware. They share the same Isuzu block but run different ECUs and wiring looms, and are not a straight ECU-compatible swap without the full electrical package.
